question: How can my student club at UC Riverside get funding for a cultural night event with food?
assumptions: Assuming the institution is University of California, Riverside (UCR) in Riverside, California, and the club is a registered student organization.
Assuming the event is held on or near campus during the 2026-27 academic year, with a planned date sometime in the coming months.

Assuming the club is seeking funds from campus sources such as the Associated Students or student government, departmental or cultural center budgets, and relevant campus offices rather than external grants.
Assuming the club needs to know both the funding application process and the rules that govern food purchases and events.

connections.explanation: Activating an ASUCR account depends on the club first holding current Student Life registration, so registration must be confirmed first.
An ASUCR-funded event must be open to all students, so food served there is offered to the public and triggers the Temporary Food Permit.
ASUCR limits food spending to $500 or 50% of the grant, while full-service catering may have to come from UC Dining Services, which could exceed that budget.
Grant money up to the $1,500 cap is paid by reimbursement requisition, which needs the Direct Deposit Form completed first.

report.directAnswer: If your club holds current Student Life registration and has activated an ASUCR account, you can likely apply for an ASUCR Organization Grant of up to $1,500 per academic year for an on-campus, one-day event open to all students. Food may take up to $500 or 50% of the grant, whichever is less. Because the event must be open to all, it will likely need a Temporary Food Permit, applied for at least 7 business days ahead, with trained food handlers. The biggest unknown is the actual ASUCR grant application form and deadline for a fall or winter event, because the sources only give the May budget deadline and account activation dates. Other options are unclear: the SIP Grant is described only for outreach events, and the CHASS-CIS cosponsorship is for CHASS faculty and graduate students, not undergraduate clubs.

keyDiscoveries.summary: ASUCR Organization Grants fund on-campus, one-day events that are open to all students.
ASUCR Organization Grants are limited to $1,500 per organization per academic year.
Up to $500 or 50% of an ASUCR event grant, whichever is less, may be used for food.
Your student organization must hold current registration before any ASUCR funding steps can proceed.
Organizations seeking ASUCR grant funding must first have activated an ASUCR account.
ASUCR FY27 accounts may be activated through Winter quarter, and access to funds expires June 4, 2027.
Registered clubs hosting a campus event where food or beverages are offered to the public, free or paid, must obtain a Temporary Food Permit.
The Temporary Food Permit application must be submitted at least 7 business days before the event.

planChangingConnections.text: Confirm your Student Life registration first, because activating an ASUCR account, which is needed for any grant, depends on it.
Since an ASUCR-funded event must be open to all students, plan on getting the Temporary Food Permit and its food safety training.
Check the catering rules before budgeting, because the $500 or 50% food limit may not cover full-service catering if UC Dining Services is required.
Expect to be reimbursed rather than paid up front, and complete the Direct Deposit Form before submitting your requisition.

uncertainties.text: The ASUCR Organization Grant application form, submission window, lead time and approval timeline for a fall or winter 2026-27 event are not established.

The food permit exemption covers only general-member or invite-only events, while ASUCR requires open events, so an open cultural night will likely need the permit, but this has not been confirmed for your event.
The Student Life food rules (UC Dining Services catering, Procurement pre-approval, permit exemption) may be outdated for 2026-27.
It is not established whether the SIP Grant covers a cultural night with food, or what its award amounts and food rules are.
No cultural center or diversity office cosponsorship open to undergraduate clubs was found, so the $1,500 cap with a food limit of $500 or 50% may be all that is available.
Several ASUCR dates, such as the May 11 budget deadline and the September 28, 2026 requisition opening, may be outdated, and the CHASS-CIS reopening notice is dated and may be stale.

nextSteps.step: Confirm that your club's Student Life registration is current for 2026-27 and renew it if it is not.

nextSteps.step: Activate your club's ASUCR account before Winter quarter ends.
nextSteps.reason: Grant funding requires an activated account, and FY27 accounts may be activated only through Winter quarter.

nextSteps.step: Ask ASUCR which application form, submission window, and approval timeline apply to an Organization Grant for your cultural night.
nextSteps.reason: The sources give only the May budget deadline and activation dates, not the grant application process.

nextSteps.step: Plan the event as on-campus, one day, and open to all students, and budget food at no more than $500 or 50% of the grant.
nextSteps.reason: These are the ASUCR conditions for grant eligibility and food spending.

nextSteps.step: Apply for a Temporary Food Permit at least 7 business days before the event, and have at least three people complete UCR Online Food Safety Training if serving hot food.
nextSteps.reason: An event open to the public with food needs the permit, and the permit and training rules carry lead times.

nextSteps.step: Ask Student Life and Procurement whether you must use UC Dining Services catering or can use an outside vendor, and get Procurement approval of the food before you buy.
nextSteps.reason: The catering rule may be outdated, and outside vendors need sponsorship and Procurement approval.
